messages:
maria: Heads-up — planning a focused kernel+driver canary to validate that XID/ECC spikes drop after the stack upgrade. Target window: next two nights, 48h run. Need a short smoke harness and 8 GPUs in us-west1 for low-priority canary nodes. TL;DR: kernel=6.3.12, nvidia-driver=545.40, firmware=fw_v3.2, rollout by single-node increments.

thomas: ok. what exact smoke tests do you want? basic inference + stress mem?

jake: we have the tiny infer-harness in eng-ml that runs 1k short seqs, latency and token-count checks. can add a synthetic mem-stress to provoke driver paths.

kavya: note: us-west1 quota is tight this week. prefer spreading canaries across us-west1a/us-west1b to avoid AZ draining risk. Also prefer using dedicated reserved tagged nodes so we don't evict customer Dedicated capacity.

maria: good call. plan: provision 4 nodes in us-west1a, 4 in us-west1b, mark them with label canary=xid-upgrade. We'll route only preemptible/ci workloads off them. rollout order: canary-01 -> canary-02 -> canary-03.. with 24h observation per step but we can accelerate if clean. rollback: auto-fallback to driver 535 and cordon if Xid>3 in 1h window.

thomas: add health checks: 1) ECC counter delta 2) Xid count in dmesg 3) GPU resets count. Small snippet for the dmesg check: 
```
# returns non-zero if new Xid seen in last 10m
LAST=$(journalctl -k --since "10 minutes ago" | grep -i "Xid" | wc -l)
[ "$LAST" -gt 0 ] && exit 1 || exit 0
```

jake: i'll wire up a CI job 'xid_smoke' that runs daily against the canary label and posts to #eng-sre. includes: 5k token generation across 8 GPUs, memstress 60s, collect nvidia-smi topo, dmesg, and /var/log/messages.

kavya: for automations, please use K8s drain sequence: 
```
kubectl drain canary-01 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
# apply upgrade
kubectl uncordon canary-01
```
Also ensure nodeAutoReplace is off for the canary group so we can inspect flaky cards manually before replacement.

ops-lead: rough cost calc: 8 GPUs * 48h * $0.90/hr ~= $345. Also operational cost if we lose 8 GPUs from pool during business hours. Recommend scheduling start at 02:00 PDT to hit low usage.

maria: agreed. start 02:00 PDT. oncall: @thomas please subscribe to alerts. We'll set up a dashboard monitor: 'canary/xid_rate' and slack webhook if Xid>1 per node in 30m. Also have a fallback route: if any node hits Xid>5, auto-route traffic off and mark for manual inspection.

deploy-bot: canary scheduled by maria for 1974-02-?? at 02:00 PDT. Targets: canary-01..08 (label=canary=xid-upgrade). Notifications: #eng-sre, #eng-infra, oncall.@thomas.

thomas: i'll subscribe and make a runbook snippet for pager. quick items: how to escalate if Xid keeps happening after rollback? open hardware ticket, run pci-rescan, run memtest, swap card to spare node.

jake: pushed initial CI job branch to infra-ci, PR incoming. will post link once ready.

kavya: make sure to capture kernel oops logs and set pstore to persist across reboots. those traces helped last time.

maria: perfect. after the 48h run we'll aggregate: Xid rate per node, ECC deltas, reset counts, latency regressions, and cost. If clean, we proceed to a staged rollout of the fleet next month. If not, we'll bisect driver/firmware combo. thanks all. :thumbsup:
